There is an absolute $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $\lambda\vdash n$ with $\lambda'_1\le n/2$ and $k>0$ satisfies $$\log D_\lambda\ge ck.
 \label{l:forest-degree-bound}$$

For every $m\ge1$ and every partition $\lambda\vdash m$, the irreducible representation $V_\lambda$ occurs in a signed tabloid representation of dimension $M$ with $$M\le D_\lambda^{C_0},\qquad C_0=2{,}000{,}000.$$

Let $E$ have $m$ elements, partitioned into $L$ buffers, and let $
u$ be a subprobability on $S_E$. Suppose that for every buffer $B$, the marginal of $
u$ on the ordered image tuple of $E\setminus B$ is pointwise at most twice its uniform marginal. If $L\ge2C_0$, then for every irreducible $\gamma$ of $S_E$, $$ rac{\|\widehat
u(\gamma)\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2}{D_\gamma}
 \le \min\{1,2D_\gamma^{-1/2}\}.
 \label{l:tabloid-normalized-hs}$$

For $\lambda\vdash 2h$ and $\alpha,\beta\vdash h$, let $c_{\alpha\beta}^\lambda$ be the multiplicity of $V_\alpha\otimes V_\beta$ in the restriction of $V_\lambda$ to $S_h\times S_h$. Then $$c_{\alpha\beta}^\lambda\le\min(D_\alpha,D_\beta).$$

One has $Z_{20}(n)\to0$. There is an absolute constant $K_0$ such that, for all $n\ge1$ and $R\ge1$, $$\label{l:degree-twenty-type-count}
 \#\{\lambda\vdash n:D_\lambda\le R\}\le K_0R^{20}.$$
One has $C_2<\infty$ and $Z_2(n)\to0$. This conclusion admits each of the tableau, hook-ratio, and second-row proofs below.
The conclusions $C_u<\infty$ and $Z_u(n)\to0$ for $u=13,16$ follow from tableau counting and $p(n)\le2^n$ alone.

For all sufficiently large $n$ and every shape of deficit $k=k(\lambda)\ge1$, $$D_\lambda\ge2^{k/2},\qquad D_\lambda\ge L(\lambda)\ge\sqrt n.$$ These inequalities and $p(k)\le2^k$ prove $C_4<\infty$ and $Z_4(n)\to0$.
One has $C_{10}<\infty$ and $Z_{10}(n)\to0$, using only the first-row interleaving construction and the bound $p(n)\le e^{3\sqrt n}$.

For every $n\ge1$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, $$\label{l:degree-sqrt-deficit-equation}
 \log D_\lambda\ge\frac{\log2}{2}\sqrt{k(\lambda)}.$$ In particular $C_{32}<\infty$ follows from this bound alone and $p(k)\le e^{3\sqrt k}$.
For $b=32$ and cap $B=4$, $$\|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac83\sqrt{C_1}\,D^{-5/16}.$$
For $b=256$ and cap $B=4$, $$\|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4\sqrt{C_{32}}D^{-1/4}.$$
If there are four blocks and the subprobability cap is $B=2$, then $$\|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2C_{1/4}^2D^{-1/8}.$$

Put $C_{\rm peel}=512^2$. Every irreducible representation of $S_m$ of degree $D$ has a one-dimensional character in its restriction to some subgroup $J$ with $[S_m:J]\le D^{C_{\rm peel}}$. At a step removing a longest first row or first column of length $r$, leaving size $s$ and degree $D'$, one has $$\label{l:peeling-ratio}
 \frac D{D'}\ge\binom{r+s}r^{1/C_{\rm peel}}.$$ The degree of the empty remainder is one.

The preceding stepwise estimate independently implies $$\sum_{\lambda\vdash m:\,D_\lambda>1}D_\lambda^{-1}\longrightarrow0.$$ Consequently, for all sufficiently large $m$ and every $Y\ge1$, $S_m$ has at most $3Y$ irreducible types of degree at most $Y$.
